analysis.title: Goldman Hikes 2027 Brent Forecast For These Two Reasons
key_insights: Goldman Sachs head of oil research Daan Struyven raised his December Brent forecast to $105/bbl from $90 and December WTI to $94 from $81.
For 2027, Goldman now expects Brent to average about $88 (from $80) and WTI about $78 (from $73).

Goldman estimates the risk premium in crude has jumped to around $27 and explains most of October's rally. Brent's fair value was little changed in September and October because global inventories, its main driver, held roughly flat.

Goldman expects markets to price a higher risk premium, citing downside risks to Mideast supply, the length of past major oil supply shocks, and a widely held view that a lasting diplomatic breakthrough will be difficult.

Goldman's two stated reasons for the upgrade: downside supply risks sustaining a large near-term risk premium, and a new global supply disruption allowance that raises disruption risk and lowers the medium-term global output forecast.
Gulf crude exports, including dark tanker fleet shipments, have recovered to at or above 2025 (pre-war) averages in recent weeks, and Mideast output continues to recover as Goldman expected.
Global visible oil inventories held steady through September and October despite a record number of tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz last month.
Goldman's chart shows the risk premium staying high for the coming months and moderating in the back half of 2027.
Historical EIA and IEA data show major oil supply shocks have often lasted for years and left lasting damage to production capacity. The article says the crisis remains in refining and diesel.
Goldman's report was published a day before Monday's diplomatic headlines, after which Brent futures fell to around $106 and WTI to roughly $97.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman raised its Brent and WTI forecasts for December 2026 and 2027 on a larger geopolitical risk premium and a new supply disruption allowance.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Goldman's higher forecast is driven by a larger geopolitical risk premium rather than a change in fundamentals.
Raised in line with the Brent forecast.
The premium is expected to moderate in the back half of 2027, so the 2027 average is below the December 2026 forecast.

risk_factors: Upside: intensified shipping attacks, damage to oil infrastructure and a more persistent risk premium could push Brent to $140.
Downside: a faster recovery in Middle East output could take Brent into the $60s in 2027.
Historical supply shocks have often lasted years and damaged production capacity.
Refining and diesel markets remain stressed.
geopolitical: Renewed supply disruption threats keep a higher geopolitical risk premium in crude even as Gulf production recovers.
A record number of tanker attacks occurred in the Strait of Hormuz in October.
Monday morning's diplomatic headlines pushed Brent down to around $106.
Many market participants see a lasting diplomatic breakthrough as difficult.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman sees substantial downside supply risks sustaining a large near-term risk premium of about $27. A new global supply disruption allowance lowers its medium-term output forecast, and past supply shocks often lasted years.
tension_points.bear_case: Gulf exports have recovered to at or above 2025 averages and global visible inventories held flat through September and October. Fair value was little changed, so the rally reflects premium rather than fundamentals. A faster Middle East recovery could take Brent into the $60s in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: 2027 average Gulf output rising 2.5mb/d above 2025 levels with the assumed global supply disruption not occurring, which would send Brent into the $60s.
